# Acute Surgical

This folder catalogs life-threatening acute surgical conditions that demand immediate medical intervention and urgent antibiotic therapy, even in the absence of fever or altered infection markers. It specifically covers ischemia, perforated hollow organs, and severe ileus, which are prioritized in the Danish Acute Surgery Database's national quality improvement initiatives. These conditions are tied to strict clinical performance indicators, such as the mandate to administer antibiotics within a three-hour window to optimize survival outcomes and prevent severe complications like sepsis.

## Pages

- [[iskaemi|Iskæmi]] — A critical ischemic condition demanding urgent antibiotic treatment to halt infection progression, categorized as a life-threatening acute surgical emergency.
- [[perforeret-hulorgan|Perforeret hulorgan]] — The rupture of a hollow viscus requiring immediate intervention to prevent sepsis, monitored under national quality indicators for rapid antibiotic and CT scan administration.
- [[svaer-ileus|Svær ileus]] — A severe bowel obstruction emergency where prompt antibiotic therapy is mandated within a three-hour window to reduce physiological stress and prevent complications.
